summary: OpenAI's lightweight Python framework for building agents and multi-agent workflows, with tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions and tracing.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: The OpenAI Agents SDK is a Python framework for building agent workflows. An agent is a model with instructions, tools, guardrails and handoffs, and the SDK runs it for you. It also supports sandbox agents that work in a container, realtime and voice agents, human-in-the-loop steps, sessions and built-in tracing.
sixtySeconds.problem: Writing the loop that calls a model, runs tools, hands off between agents and keeps history is repetitive. The SDK provides those pieces with a small API.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a small, provider-agnostic API that supports the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs and many other models.

overview: Install with pip or uv. Optional extras add voice support, Redis sessions and Docker sandboxes.
Set OPENAI_API_KEY, create an Agent with a name and instructions, and run it with Runner.run_sync. Agents can call function tools, MCP tools and hosted tools, and hand work to other agents.
There are four main ways to run agents: text, sandbox, realtime and voice. Tracing lets you view and debug runs. It is MIT licensed; a JavaScript/TypeScript version is in a separate repo.

tutorial.title: Run your first text agent

steps.title: Create the agent
steps.body: from agents import Agent, Runner, then Agent(name="Assistant", instructions="You are a helpful assistant").

steps.title: Run it
steps.body: Runner.run_sync(agent, "Write a haiku about recursion in programming.").

tutorial.expected: A short haiku printed in your terminal.
